title: Anime Aerial Mage Battle
description: A highly sophisticated prompt for a cinematic anime sequence featuring a pink-haired mage battling a dragon above a magical city.
promptText: High-quality anime footage. High-density 3D toon / cel-look. A cinematic high-fantasy aerial battle set in the skies above a massive magical city after the rain. A pink-haired girl mage is chased by a giant black dragon, escaping through towers at high speed. Just as the dragon closes in to the limit, she spreads her cloak wide to decelerate sharply, rolling her body to face the dragon directly. From a multi-layered convergence gate in her right palm, she fires a high-output beam into the center of the dragon's chest as it approaches at high relative speed, causing it to disintegrate into black ash and mana particles. [Character Identity Consistency and Role of Reference Images] image1 is the primary reference for the protagonist's face and identity. Maintain a soft oval face, small chin, large blue-violet to purple-pink eyes with layered irises and white catchlights, delicate eye area, long coral-pink twin tails, light bangs, lavender flowers on both sides, and black-purple ribbons with gold decorations throughout. image2 is the reference for the protagonist's outfit, decorations, full-body design, and equipment. Maintain a slender and petite build, a dark navy to purple gold-edged cloak, a white frilled blouse, a black-purple corset, a purple multi-layered pleated skirt, white knee-highs, dark purple boots with metal fittings, a waist belt, amethyst crystals, magic potions, and a grimoire with gold decorations. If references conflict, prioritize image1 for the face, eyes, irises, bangs, hair color, and hair ornaments; prioritize image2 for the outfit, decorations, build, equipment, and full-body silhouette. These two images are for appearance reference only; do not include backgrounds, compositions, poses, white backgrounds, setting sheet borders, text, or split layouts in the video. The only elements allowed to change are focused facial expressions, eye direction, breathing, flying posture, and the natural movement of hair, cloak, and skirt. Prevent face averaging, feature blending, outfit swapping, proliferation of equipment, clones, replicas, or additional characters. [Art Style Fix: High-Density 3D Toon / Cel-look] This style fix does not override character identity consistency. Thin, delicate colored outlines. Clear two- to three-tone cel shading on the face, hair, outfit, and equipment with transparent mid-shadows. Multi-layered highlights on the eyes and hair. Use pink, lavender, dark navy, purple, and gold as the protagonist's color axes, ensuring skin tones remain clear. Distinguish textures like cloth, frills, leather, metal, amethyst, wet stone, and glass with different reflections and roughness. Movie-quality key animation, high-quality compositing, transparent lighting, and dense background art. Only magic should use high-brightness graphic anime VFX, volumetric light, additive emission, refractive waves, and directional motion blur. Avoid thick black outlines, flat single-layer cel shadows, generic 3D anime faces, smooth plastic CG, low-density backgrounds, semi-realism, realism, dull colors, or mixed art styles. [Maintained Flight Posture and Trajectory] The basic posture for the entire sequence is a high-speed pass, leaning forward until the body is almost horizontal, viewed from a low side angle. Both legs are kept together and extended long behind, with toes pointing straight back in the direction of travel. The cloak billows and spreads wide behind from the back, and the twin tails are pulled straight back in the same direction as the legs. The camera is placed lower than the protagonist, conveying speed through the fast-moving foreground mist, rain, and tower edges. This posture and trajectory must be maintained across all cuts. [Protagonist's Propulsion Fix] The protagonist flies unaided, not on a flying machine or vehicle. Do not attach vents, nozzles, or propulsion devices to the back, waist, or soles of the feet. Do not create light beams or flame pillars extending long from a single point behind. Propulsion is shown only through the following three methods: First, at the moment of acceleration, a single pale purple-pink magic circle appears in the air behind the protagonist's feet. Immediately after the soles of the shoes kick that surface, the circle shatters into particles, and the reaction pushes the body forward. The circle disappears immediately after the kick and leaves no pillar of light behind. Second, during flight, thin purple-pink mana streamlines flow backwards in layers along the body's silhouette. These streamlines are not merged into a single bundle but extend thinly from the edges of the hair, cloak, arms, and legs, quickly dissolving into the air. Third, on the path passed through, only thin residual light streaks and particles remain briefly before disappearing. Streamlines and residual streaks must always flow straight back relative to the direction of travel. In acceleration, the torso leans forward and the legs extend back; in deceleration, the streamlines shrink thinly and the chest rises. In turns, the shoulders and waist lean first to bank the whole body sideways, curving along an arc inside the bank angle. The twin tails, cloak, and skirt always flow straight back, swelling to the outside of the arc only during turns. [Protagonist's Equipment Fix] Only one grimoire. Maintain the same binding and thickness with gold decorations, fixed in a holder on the left waist and closed throughout. Amethyst crystals and magic potions are also kept connected to the belt. All attacks are issued from the right palm and not fired from the grimoire or potions. Do not introduce new items, wings, or a second book not in image2. [Black Dragon Fix] The enemy is a single giant black four-legged wyvern. Approximately four times the protagonist's total length. One head, two horns, two glowing bluish-white eyes, a continuous neck and torso, four legs, and three claws on each foot. One pair of wings, two in total. Each wing consists of wing bones and membranes continuous from the base of the back. One tail, continuous from the back of the waist to the base, scales, and tip without branching. Flight is achieved by downstrokes of the wings to move forward, steering with the neck and single tail, and banking the whole body into the inner arc during turns. Avoid flying where the torso doesn't move while only the wings flap. The impact point is a single point on the scales in the center of the chest. Do not create extra heads, horns, legs, wings, or tails. [Setting] The sky over a massive magical city after the rain. Magical towers and spires reaching for the heavens, thin arch bridges, aerial corridors, floating turrets, giant crystal pillars, mana lamps, low-hanging rain clouds, and layers of mist are densely arranged as obstacles along the flight path. Below, wet cobblestone avenues and glowing magical waterways shine thinly. City lights are cyan, royal blue, violet, purple, and a small amount of magenta. Background lighting is one step darker than the protagonist, making her pink, lavender, purple, and gold inherent colors the main focus. Do not place readable magical text; only abstract geometric patterns on the surfaces of towers or crystals should glow faintly. [Space and Continuity] Throughout the sequence, the protagonist and the black dragon are on the same single flight path. In Cuts 1 to 3, the protagonist is at the front of the line and the black dragon is behind, both moving from the back of the screen to the front, and from the top right to the bottom left. In Cut 4, only the protagonist decelerates rapidly to reverse her facing direction. The front-back positioning and movement direction on screen are maintained, and the left-right orientation of the protagonist and the dragon are not swapped. Cuts 4 to 6 align the right palm, the center of the convergence gate, the beam, and the center of the dragon's chest in a straight line. The distance between the two closes continuously in Cuts 1 to 3, becomes the shortest during the sudden deceleration in Cut 4, and continues to close until contact in Cut 5. In adjacent cuts, at least two of the following must change: camera height, distance to the protagonist, character size on screen, or the background's vanishing axis. The camera must always be moved with a specific purpose—showing the contact point, showing the direction of force, returning a facial payoff, or updating the spatial relationship and distance change between the two—and not substitute character movement for camera movement. All actions should have natural acceleration, deceleration, inertia, and parallax. Cut 1: Chased. Begin from a low side-rear angle at wing height. The protagonist is slightly above the center of the screen, and the black dragon emerges from the mist in the background, drawing closer with each large downstroke of its wings. The protagonist leans her shoulders and waist to the right, kicks a single magic circle that appears behind her feet to accelerate into a gap between towers. The circle shatters and scatters immediately after being kicked. Raindrops and mist flow backwards past the body, and the hair and cloak are pulled straight back. The black dragon extends its neck and opens its jaws, snapping them shut just behind the protagonist's back. Always leave a small gap between the fangs and the back, never letting them touch the protagonist. The impact of the snap causes the surrounding mist to burst left and right, and the protagonist's body dips once due to the air currents. The protagonist maintains that momentum, kicks another circle to compensate for the dip, and pulls ahead. The camera follows the protagonist while grazing the outside of the dragon's jaw, showing the closing distance in the same frame. Cut 2: Weaving Through the Tower Gaps. A camera retreating in the direction of travel, in front of the protagonist. Capture both the protagonist's face and the dragon's head looming behind in the same frame. The protagonist ducks under a thin arch bridge, leans her shoulders to the left at the next spire, and passes through a narrow gap between towers by tilting her body sideways. The waist and legs follow with a delay, and the hem of the skirt grazes the corner of the stone. The black dragon cannot fit through the same gap and crashes shoulder-first into the arch bridge. Stone fragments and dust scatter backwards, and broken bridge girders fall below. The dragon does not lose speed, recovering its posture and continuing the chase with the momentum of the impact. The protagonist's face is kept at a distance where it can be read from the front, with her bangs pushed up by the wind and rain hitting her cheeks. The camera passes through the debris and hands off to the next shot as the distance closes further. Cut 3: Closest Approach and Dive Evasion. From a low side view, showing only the distance between the two with a crystal pillar in the foreground. The black dragon extends its right front leg, spreading its three claws to reach for the protagonist's back. There is a clear gap between the claw tips and the protagonist's back, and both the protagonist and her outfit remain unharmed. Just before the claws reach, the protagonist stops kicking, momentarily letting the mana streamlines around her body thin out, and dives sharply while rolling vertically from the shoulders. The claws strike the crystal pillar behind instead of the protagonist; only after contact does the surface of the pillar shatter into sparks and crystal shards, and the dragon's front leg recoils. The protagonist maintains the speed gained from the dive, crosses the light of the magical waterway below, and transitions back to a climb. The black dragon banks into the inner arc, staying glued directly behind and closing the distance to the absolute minimum. Expressions change in this order: first, the irises of both eyes brighten and narrow; next, the eyebrows draw toward the center; then, the eyelids narrow slightly; after that, the mouth is tightly set; and finally, the gaze is directed over the shoulder at the center of the dragon's chest. Cut 4: Rapid Deceleration and Reversal. A close-range shot over the protagonist's shoulder, with the camera orbiting along with the body's rotation. The protagonist opens both arms to spread her cloak to its maximum. The cloak catches the air and strains backwards, the mana streamlines shrink rapidly, the chest rises, the upper body decelerates first, and the waist and legs are sent forward by inertia. Maintaining that deceleration, she half-turns her body on the axis of the shoulders and waist, facing her face, chest, and right palm toward the black dragon while her back is still oriented in the direction of travel. The cloak flips and flows behind the body, and the twin tails overtake the side of the face before settling back. The dragon cannot decelerate and charges head-on with its jaws open and chest centered. The distance between the two closes rapidly due to relative speed. An incomplete concentric ring gate with two to four layers is formed in front of the right palm, featuring a white glowing core, cyan outer light, and thin purple-pink edges. Each ring is spaced front-to-back, counter-rotating at different speeds, with short ticks, radial lines, and blue-violet lightning converging on the firing axis. The circles are not contained within the frame but are significantly cropped. The left hand supports the outside of the right wrist, showing the connection of the palm, wrist, elbow, and shoulder, without the rings obscuring the whole arm. The amethyst light of the palm pulses strongly twice, and on the second pulse, the rings compress. The face remains in the dark gaps, not hidden by the arcs. Cut 5: Maximum Output Beam and Single-Frame Giant Impact. A camera moving from above and behind the dragon along the beam axis toward the impact point. A thick beam occupying 35 to 45 percent of the outer diameter is fired from the compression gate. A high-density white to pale pink core, a thick hot pink and magenta outer shell, a violet middle layer, a thin cyan-white edge, and blue-violet electric arcs. Do not thin it to a mere rod. Maintain the thickness, brightness, and axis continuously even after reaching maximum output. Three compression waves travel sequentially inside the beam from the muzzle to the chest center; as each wave passes, the outer shell expands, pushing aside the surrounding rain, mist, and clouds. Until just before the first wave arrives, the dragon's chest scales, wing membranes, and tail remain intact, with no cracks, glow, or collapse shown beforehand. Only at the exact moment the first wave contacts the scales in the center of the chest does that point indent. Only after contact do localized sparks scatter, the scales creak, the open wing membranes lose tension and ripple, and the shock is transmitted with a delay to the neck and single tail. The dragon's forward speed drops, but it is still pushed forward by inertia. In the same frame that the third compression wave reaches the chest, the entire beam is completely erased from muzzle to impact point. Do not leave a thin afterglow. In that same frame, an incandescent nucleus appears in the center of the chest, and a localized hemispherical shock dome expands once. The dome immediately ruptures, and a giant flame-like aura erupts three-dimensionally upwards and to the sides from the incandescent nucleus. The aura separates and leaves behind internal hot pink and magenta, middle layers of violet and purple, and outer edges of royal blue and cyan. Sharp flame tips, thick bands of volumetric light, transparent refractive waves, thin lightning, and outward-bound speed lines are deployed at different depths and speeds in the foreground, midground, and background. Each tongue of flame varies in size, angle, depth, and rise. Integrate the previously straight beam axis, the radially extending flame tongues, the circumferentially spreading shock rings, and the upward-rising turbulence into the same impact point at the center of the chest to show them as a single force. Limit pure white to the area around the impact nucleus, leaving colors outside the incandescent core. Maintain the high-saturation color planes of hot pink, magenta, and cyan, which occupy most of the screen, for multiple frames after the initial flash before they decay. Do not white out the entire screen. At the same moment, multiple objects react: rain clouds are pushed outward in a ring from the impact point, mist swirls and scatters, black scale fragments and stone debris fly, the protagonist's hair is blown violently back, the pillars and mana lamps below flicker, and the camera is pushed back. The protagonist maintains her posture even within the blast. Keeping her right palm at chest height, she absorbs and redirects the shock through the palm, wrist, elbow, shoulder, and waist in sequence, kicks a single circle behind her feet to hold her ground in mid-air against the pushback, and carries that counter-force directly into the next stance, returning her left hand to the front of her body. Immediately after, a mass of gray-purple smoke and black scales with varying sizes, dark cavities, internal purple light, swirls, and rising speed differences overlaps in the foreground, completely hiding the dragon's head, torso, legs, wings, and tail. At the end of this cut, the protagonist remains in a hovering posture in the foreground, her body oriented toward the dragon in the smoke, handing off that posture and position to the next cut. Cut 6: Collapse into Black Ash and Sky's End. The camera moves to a medium-range shot over the protagonist's right shoulder with a gap in the smoke in the foreground, keeping the protagonist in the front and the collapsing dragon in the back within the same frame. The protagonist inherits the hovering posture, right palm height, and body orientation from the previous cut. As the wind splits the center of the smoke, the black dragon is shown with its chest impact point toward us, wings half-folded as it stalls and begins a gentle fall with its neck drooping. Do not return it to a climb or a re-charge. Amethyst and cyan-white mana cracks run across the entire body along the seams of the scales, starting from the center of the chest. The moment a crack reaches the shoulder, the upper body lurches forward once, and short sparks scatter from the edges of the broken scales. The edges of the black scales touched by the cracks carbonize and unravel into thin black ash, turning into microscopic purple, magenta, and cyan mana particles. The disintegration begins from the wingtips and tail tip, proceeding continuously to the wing membranes, bones, tail, limbs, torso, neck, and head. Do not physically sever wings or the tail; instead, they particle-ize as holes expand from the outside of the connected silhouette inward. The black ash billows into a rising vortex, and the mana particles draw short spirals before losing their light. Finally, the mana core in the chest, the two horns, and the bluish-white light in both eyes shatter into particles, and both the body and falling debris vanish completely. Do not leave a corpse falling to the ground. The protagonist does not move to pursue, maintaining her hover while letting the counter-force flow from her right arm to her waist. The end is a single image of the battle's result. The protagonist in the foreground maintains a mid-shot size from the chest up, remaining at a distance where her face, eyes, hair ornaments, and cloak can be read. Behind her, only the sky where the dragon once was remains, with a ring of displaced rain clouds and fading black ash and purple-cyan particles drifting. The protagonist lowers her right palm a few centimeters while remaining in a guard stance; the mana streamlines around her body thin out and calm down, and her twin tails and cloak begin to hang down with her breath. The final vortex of black ash rises in front of the lens; cut the frame as soon as that vortex clears the top edge of the screen and it's clear that neither the dragon's form nor any falling shadow remains anywhere. Do not transition to a long victory pose or additional facial close-ups. [Audio] No dialogue, singing, or BGM. Sounds must never play before the corresponding contact or action. Cut 1 features the short explosive sound of kicking the magic circle, the high-pitched wind whistling of the mana streamlines flowing around the body, the low explosive sound of the dragon's wings beating the air, the hard collision sound of the jaws snapping fangs together, the sound of fabric whipping in the air currents, and the protagonist's short breath. Cut 2 features the sound of air compression the moment she passes through the tower gap, the scraping sound of the skirt hem against the stone, the crushing sound of stone as the dragon's shoulder hits the arch bridge, and the gritty sound of falling masonry and dust. Cut 3 features a brief silent interval when she stops kicking and the streamlines break, the sound of fabric wrapping as the body rolls vertically, the hard, clear crushing sound and high-pitched scattering of crystal shards when the claws hit the crystal pillar, and the short explosive sound of kicking the circle to re-ascend. Cut 4 features the loud fabric snap of the cloak catching the air, the wind noise dropping as she decelerates, the dragon's approaching low growl and wing beats, the high-pitched mana resonance and low convergence sound of the rings, and the pulsing sound from the palm. Cut 5 maintains the thick, continuous roar of compressed mana, synchronizing the scraping sound of hard scales and low-frequency mana impact sounds as each of the three compression waves hits the chest scales. Synchronize the resonant burst of the mana dome, the outward wind pressure, the low growl of the clouds being torn, and the collision sounds of stone and black scale fragments to the moment of contact, placing the protagonist's short breath at the end of the firing hold. Cut 6 synchronizes the fine scraping sound of dry scales unraveling into ash, the wind rustle of the black ash, and the high-pitched crystalline sound of mana particles to the disappearance of each part. Stop the low tones the moment the final core vanishes, leaving only the sound of the wind in the upper atmosphere and the protagonist's quiet breathing for a short moment. [Critical Failure Prevention] No text, subtitles, logos, watermarks, or setting sheet UI. No additional characters, second wizards, or clones. Do not give the protagonist wings, vehicles, brooms, or mechanical devices. No vents, nozzles, propulsion gear, or jet-like pillars of light or fire from a single point on the back or soles of the feet. No sliding/hovering without any indication of propulsion, no flying where the streamlines and direction of travel don't match, and no turns without banking. The dragon's fangs and claws must never touch the protagonist's body. No injuries or torn clothing for the protagonist. No shortening, thinning, flickering, mid-way attenuation, premature explosion, or long simultaneous display of the beam and explosion, and no residual lasers. No symmetrical, flat flower-shaped explosions, no uniform-sized round smoke clouds, and no pastel colors. Do not white out the whole screen. Do not composite the dragon in front of the smoke. Do not show the dragon before the smoke clears. No recovery, instantaneous disappearance, transparency, severed wings or tails, or multiple tails for the dragon. Do not make the protagonist's face a generic or expressionless surface. No halos, light spots adhering to the face, or thick borders crossing the face. Do not shrink the protagonist to a tiny dot in the background at the end.

title: Red Bull F1 Racing Commercial
description: A high-end cinematic commercial prompt transitioning a tired office worker into a professional Formula 1 driver.
promptText: Create a cinematic high-end commercial showing a young professional working at his desk in a modern luxury office. He looks focused and slightly tired while working on his computer. Cut to a close-up as he grabs and drinks an ice-cold Red Bull energy drink. After taking a sip, the atmosphere transforms dramatically — fast-paced cinematic transition into a Formula 1 racing environment. Reveal the same man now as a professional Red Bull Racing Formula 1 driver, wearing a detailed racing helmet and suit, sitting inside an F1 car on the starting grid. Show intense close-ups of his determined eyes, hands gripping the steering wheel, and the engine roaring to life. Transition into dynamic onboard racing shots at high speed around a professional circuit, with dramatic camera movement, motion blur, realistic lighting, stadium crowds, and cinematic depth of field. End with a powerful first-person cockpit shot speeding down the track with the Red Bull branding clearly visible. Photorealistic, premium commercial aesthetic, seamless transitions, energetic pacing, realistic physics, 4K, cinematic lighting, ultra-detailed.

title: Casual Smartphone Tailgate Party Footage
description: An authentic smartphone-style home video montage of a stadium parking lot tailgate party, using a reference photo to maintain character consistency.
promptText:
Super casual real smartphone home video footage, lively tailgate party in a stadium parking lot before a football game, natural mobile phone camera with slight authentic handheld shake, normal frame rate with smooth natural motion, rapidfire montage with constant quick jump cuts every 1-2 seconds like scrolling through phone memories, unpolished authentic phone recording of friends grilling, cheering and hanging out near cars, pure raw home video feel, no cinematic polish or heavy effects.
Use the provided reference photo as the strict ONLY visual reference for the main woman. Maintain her exact appearance with zero deviation. Generate a mixed group of friends around her at the tailgate, cars, coolers and team gear visible.
0-2.5s: Shaky rapid cuts — main woman laughing near a car trunk, tailgate setup behind her, quick flashes of friends grilling.
2.5-5s: Abrupt jump cuts — close-up of her smiling while holding a drink, then friends tossing a football around.
5-7.5s: Fast shaky — she chats animatedly, cheering with friends, stadium visible in the distance.
7.5-10s: Quick cut close-up — excited smile toward camera, then jump to her laughing with friends near the cooler.
10-12.5s: Abrupt edit — group cheering together, high-fiving, casual toast with cans.
12.5-15s: Final rapid transition — main woman relaxed among friends, soft smile, calm tailgate memory ending with slight natural phone sway.
Natural smartphone video quality, slight real handheld shake, smooth normal frame rate motion with no low fps or choppy artifacts, authentic casual interactions and physics, stable main character consistency, no pro stabilization or effects.

title: Ancient Temple Explorer Adventure One-Shot
description: A professional 30-second continuous adventure sequence prompt featuring an explorer navigating complex mechanical traps in an ancient underground temple.
promptText:
[Generation Target]
@img1 Generate a 30-second one-shot adventure action film. The main subject is a male explorer, and the core event is a continuous sequence of breaking through mechanical traps in an underground temple to finally reach the treasure. No audience, no studio; a realistic ancient ruin.

[Global Settings]
1. Environment/Texture: Inside an ancient underground temple. Mossy giant stone walls, cracked stone floors, narrow light beams from ceiling gaps, orange torchlight on walls. Dust floating in the air. Extremely realistic physical textures—stone wear, leather scratches, sweat, and dirt.
2. Visual Style: Adventure movie live-action feel, cinematic, shallow depth of field, mixed lighting of warm torch tones and cold light beams, film grain.
3. Camera Language: No-cut one-shot, Steadicam tracking. Never center the character—always maintain off-center composition at left/right thirds, leave lead space in the direction of movement, alternating between side profiles and 3/4 rear angles by segment.
4. Character: East Asian male explorer in his 30s. Black short hair, tanned skin, old brown leather jacket, khaki shirt, wide-brimmed brown Fedora-style hat, leather messenger bag across shoulders, leather gloves, holding a torch in one hand. Same person, same clothing throughout.
5. Performance Core: Immediate reflex actions at the moment traps trigger, heavy breathing, short look back after landing, a restrained smile in front of the treasure.
6. Prohibitions: No subtitles or text on screen, no BGM, no arbitrary cuts, no audience/host/studio lights/neon/game show elements, no gore, no centering the character.

[Timestamp Storyboard]
Stage 1: 0-5s [Entry and First Trap]
Man holding a torch passes through a narrow stone door—camera follows at 3/4 rear angle from the right third. Second step, a stone slab clicks and sinks; darts shoot continuously from wall holes. Man dives and rolls forward; darts hit the wall behind.
End state: Man on one knee, darts pinned in the wall behind him. Torch still in hand.

Stage 2: 5-12s [Underground Waterway Stones]
Continuation: Same clothing, torch maintained. Floor ends at a black underground waterway—six square stones arranged in a zigzag. Man jumps across. Each stone sinks slowly as he steps, bubbles rise; he leaps before it sinks. Side profile tracking at water level—man at left third with lead space.
Emotion: This jump is calculated progress, not acrobatics—eyes always on the next stone.
End state: Man lands on the opposite platform; the last stone sinks completely.

Stage 3: 12-18s [Pendulum Blade Corridor]
Three giant half-moon stone pendulums swing from the ceiling. Man observes the rhythm for one beat, then passes through in a stop-dash-stop rhythm. For the last one, he leans back as it grazes his chest. Side tracking along corridor wall; pendulums periodically cross the foreground.
End state: Man at corridor end, pendulums still swinging behind him.

Stage 4: 18-24s [Collapsing Bridge Sprint]
Outside an archway, an old stone bridge spans an abyss. As he takes the first step, slabs begin to collapse from the rear. Man sprints—collapse follows his heels. Leaps at bridge end, rolls onto ground. 3/4 rear low-angle chase; man at right third, collapsing bridge fills the left.
End state: Man lands in a crouch; bridge fully collapsed into the abyss.

Stage 5: 24-30s [Treasure Room]
Man rises; on a stone platform, a light beam illuminates a small gold idol with gems. He approaches, carefully cradling the idol. The temple rumbles, dust falls. He puts the idol in his bag, turns to camera with a restrained smile—ends in a 3/4 side medium-close shot at the left third.
Emotion: The smile is relief and excitement.
End state: Idol in bag, man's face lit by torch, dust falling.

[Consistency Maintenance]
Maintain same character/clothing/props (torch, bag, hat) throughout. Direction of travel is left to right. Maintain lighting logic. Audio: SFX and ambient only—footsteps, stone friction, water, pendulum wind, heavy breathing. Strictly no subtitles, BGM, or cuts.

title: Mediterranean Musical Scene Long Take
description: A detailed cinematic prompt for a photorealistic romantic musical sequence on a Mediterranean promenade, maintaining character consistency from multiple reference images.
promptText: Use <<<image_1>>> as the SOLE appearance reference for the FEMALE LEAD and <<<image_2>>>as the SOLE appearance reference for the MALE LEAD. Preserve their exact facial identity, facial structure, hairstyle, hair color, body proportions, outfits, shoes, accessories, and clothing colors in every frame. Do NOT redesign, recolor, replace, modify, simplify, or add anything to their clothing or accessories. The two leads must remain unmistakably the same people throughout the entire video. No face morphing, identity drift, hairstyle changes, body changes, wardrobe changes, or age changes. EXTRAS: Exactly 10–14 ensemble dancers. They must have completely different faces from both leads. Do not make any extra resemble either lead. Diverse ages and ethnicities. Wardrobe: colorful pastel summer clothing — sunflower yellow, sky blue, coral, mint, soft pink, cream — including flowing summer dresses, light shirts, trousers, and tailored suits. Their styling should feel like a vibrant modern interpretation of a classic Hollywood musical. Natural fabric movement, realistic hair movement, and varied individual body language. Extras must never look duplicated or cloned. === FORMAT === Premium 30-second cinematic romantic musical film. 16:9 landscape. Fully photorealistic. ONE continuous flowing cinematic take with NO visible cuts. The entire video must feel alive, energetic, romantic, spontaneous, and human. There must be NO dull moments, no empty stretches, no static compositions, no performer standing motionless, and no long shots where nothing meaningful happens. Something should always be evolving through character movement, camera movement, background action, facial expression, choreography, environment, or music. Native 16:9 composition. No letterboxing. No black bars. No artificial AI-video aesthetic. The final result should feel like a real premium musical scene filmed on location with professional actors, dancers, cinematographers, and musicians. === LOCATION / ENVIRONMENT === Set the entire scene on a beautiful Mediterranean-style seaside promenade during a pleasant summer morning. A wide elegant pedestrian promenade runs alongside a sparkling blue sea. Warm cream-colored stone buildings line one side of the promenade. Small stylish cafés with outdoor tables and umbrellas open onto the walkway. Palm trees and Mediterranean plants move gently in the sea breeze. A low stone sea wall runs along the waterfront. Small sailboats and distant boats are visible on the horizon. A few colorful awnings, flower planters, bicycles, and café chairs create natural environmental detail. The location should feel upscale, cinematic, lived-in, and authentic rather than touristy or artificial. The sea provides bright atmospheric depth behind the performers. The promenade should have enough space for the leads and dancers to move naturally without feeling crowded. The environment itself should constantly provide subtle visual movement: palm leaves moving in the breeze, distant boats drifting, pedestrians walking, café activity, fabric moving, dancers crossing the promenade, and sunlight reflecting softly from the water. Do not make the background chaotic. The leads remain the visual focus. === MUSIC — 30-SECOND ROMANTIC ENERGY ARC === Create an ORIGINAL romantic cinematic pop song at approximately 108 BPM. Major key. Warm, joyful, playful, flirtatious, uplifting, and emotionally sincere. The song should feel romantic without becoming slow, sad, overly sentimental, or theatrical. • Setting: Backyard terrace of a modern private residence in Holosiiv, Kyiv, Ukraine, with light concrete walls, vertical wood slats, floor-to-ceiling glass doors, birch, and pine trees.
• Ambient sound: Distant city traffic, rustling leaves, gentle breeze, clear character breathing and sobbing. Ambient sound dips when dialogue occurs.
• Characters:
  Tetiana (corresponds to @Image1): consistent face, grey-green eyes, center-parted long straight black hair, black satin midi dress, black strappy heels. Voice is mid-high range, pace changes from restrained to frantic, volume rises to a shout, ending broken by tears. Consistent across all shots.
  Vova (corresponds to @Image2): consistent face, brown eyes, short brown textured hair, light stubble, black suit, open-collar white shirt, black leather shoes. Voice is mid-low range, starts low then becomes loud and curt. Consistent across all shots.
• Spatial Blocking: Tetiana stands on the right, garden behind her. Vova stands on the left, glass door behind him. Two steps apart. Camera maintains a strict 180-degree axis for eye-line continuity.
• Dialogue: Natural English

Sequence List:
Shot 1 (0s-1.2s) Establishing
• Camera: Medium two-shot, eye level, 90-degree profile, deep focus.
• Movement: Non-professional handheld, lateral drift of 30cm between them with one slight late framing correction.
• Action: Tetiana takes a half-step toward Vova, fists at her sides, chest rising rapidly, eyes filling with tears. Vova's shoulders tense, jaw tightens. In the last 0.2s, Tetiana takes a sharp breath and begins the first line.
• Exit: Tetiana's voice leads into the next angle.

Shot 2 (1.2s-4.5s) Request Outburst
• Camera: Close-up on Tetiana over Vova's left shoulder, eye level, 0-degree front. Vova's shoulder, Tetiana's face, and the background garden all stay sharp.
• Movement: Unstable handheld, pushes 15cm toward Tetiana, framing shifts slightly as her volume peaks.
• Action: Tetiana swallows, lower lip quivers, brows knit inward and up. Nostrils flare at 'dream', first tear rolls down right cheek at 'forever'. Tear has realistic surface tension reflecting white sky light. Stares fixedly at Vova.
• Dialogue: Tetiana says in a rising, cracking voice: 'Vova, I want a red panda! It's been my dream forever!'
• Exit: Last word carries into the first 0.3s of Vova's reaction shot.

Shot 3 (4.5s-8.5s) Refutation
• Camera: Medium close-up on Vova over Tetiana's right shoulder, eye level, 45-degree three-quarter view, all planes sharp.
• Movement: Handheld push 12cm, adding small lateral jitters as Vova's volume rises.
• Action: Vova blinks hard as the last word ends, jaw muscles clench, short nasal inhale. Voice starts low then turns loud and curt, right palm briefly gestures toward the house. Lips tight at the end. Tetiana's next line cuts in during the last 0.2s.
• Dialogue: Vova says in a voice turning from low to loud: 'We already have a cat and a Labrador! Our home is not a zoo!'
• Exit: Tetiana's shout overlaps Vova's final reaction.

Shot 4 (8.5s-11s) Losing Control
• Camera: Extreme close-up on Tetiana over Vova's shoulder, 10-degree low angle, 0-degree front, deep focus. Wet lashes, tear tracks, pores, and Vova's shoulder all sharp.
• Movement: Irregular handheld push 10cm, framing briefly drifts right during the first shout, manually corrected back to eyes.
• Action: Tetiana's eyes widen, tears flow continuously, nose reddens, mouth pulls down, shoulders twitch with every breath. First line is shouted, second voice breaks. Lips stay open at the end with one shaky breath.
• Dialogue: Tetiana says in a high, tearful volume: 'It's my dream! Why don't you care?'
• Exit: Vova's 'Tania' leads the audio into the next shot while still on Tetiana's face.

Shot 5 (11s-13.5s) Boundaries
• Camera: Close-up on Vova over Tetiana's right shoulder, 5-degree high angle, 45-degree three-quarter view, deep focus.
• Movement: Starts static, then slow 10cm push, maintaining low-amplitude phone handheld breathing.
• Action: Vova maintains eye contact, nostrils flare, jaw tensed. Volume rises at 'red panda', drops at 'pet'. Eyes drop toward Tetiana's tears at the end, lips tight.
• Dialogue: Vova says in a loud but restrained voice: 'Tania, a red panda is not a pet!'
• Exit: Last word carries into Tetiana's final reaction.

Shot 6 (13.5s-15s) Breakdown
• Camera: Extreme close-up on Tetiana's eyes and mouth, eye level, 0-degree front. Vova's shoulder and the background remain sharp.
• Movement: Handheld push stops, retaining only natural micro-jitter.
• Action: After the last word, Tetiana's lower lip loses control, corners of the mouth pull down, shoulders slump forward into a suppressed sob. New tear forms on lower lid and follows old track. Vova raises a hand in the foreground but stops mid-air. Ambient sound drops to near silence for one beat before traffic resumes.
• Exit: Lingers on Tetiana's unable-to-speak breath.

Technical Constraints:
• Identity, clothing, height ratio, position, lighting direction, exposure, and environment remain consistent across all shots.
• Each shot is a continuous take; editing follows the 180-degree rule.
• f/16 deep focus throughout; foreground, midground, and background remain sharp.
• Pro-Mist filter only affects highlights; facial structure and edges remain sharp.
• All English dialogue accurately lip-synced.
• Red panda is only mentioned; visuals contain only Tetiana and Vova.
• No subtitles, text, watermarks, logos, music, extra dialogue, or morphing.

Priority Generation: Shot 4 (voice break), Shot 6 (tear movement, final sob, Vova's hand).

title: Seoul Night Market FPV Food Tour
description: A continuous FPV drone-style video prompt capturing the atmosphere of a Seoul night market and a woman enjoying spicy tteokbokki.
promptText: One single CONTINUOUS FPV shot, no cuts, no edits, one unbroken take. Real-time speed throughout, controlled and fluid — never frantic. Only ever moves forward in time — never loops, reverses or rewinds. NO slow motion except one half-second beat at the first bite, then an instant snap back to full speed. The image is clean and fully exposed edge to edge in every frame, all four corners as sharp and bright as the centre — no vignette, no dark frame edges, no goggle mask, no lens artefacts of any kind. The camera is INVISIBLE — no shadow or reflection ever appears in frame; it stirs no steam and leaves no trace. The take runs continuously until time runs out, still inside the market. CINEMATIC CAPTURE Clean sharp glass, 180-degree shutter with natural motion blur only on genuinely fast movement, fine grain, warm tungsten and red-neon colour over rich night tones held at natural saturation, skin tones true and unpushed, light filling the frame fully into all four corners — the texture of night street footage shot on a cinema camera in flight, NOT a game engine, NOT animation. The camera opens already inside a busy open-air Seoul night food market, moving between the stalls at a steady 20 km/h — a low roof of tangled bulbs and hanging plastic sheeting overhead, steam and grill smoke pouring across the aisle from every side, radios and shouting under it. It passes a man at arm's length turning skewers over coals and fanning the smoke away with a cardboard flap, swings around a couple leaning over a shared paper tray of fried chicken who step back laughing to let it by, and drifts past a grandmother at a folding table cracking mussels open with a knife and dropping the shells into a bucket. A stray dog trots the length of the aisle ahead of it. The camera turns into a glowing orange stall at the end of the row and settles into one smooth unbroken orbit around a young Korean woman in her twenties on a plastic stool at the counter — round warm face, short black bob with a red clip, cream puffer jacket beaded with rain — as the vendor, a broad woman in her sixties in a floral apron, ladles tteokbokki into a paper bowl in front of her. The camera drifts past her shoulder to the grill where skewers sizzle and snap in oil, then comes back as she lifts the first rice cake on a wooden skewer, thick red sauce clinging to it in uneven runs, and blows on it once — and the frame holds one half-second on her face as she takes the bite: her eyes close and her cheeks puff against the heat. Snap back to full speed. She laughs through her nose immediately, still chewing, fanning her open mouth with one hand and stamping one foot. The camera pulls wide enough to hold them both as the vendor laughs behind the counter and a man waiting behind her laughs too, and the woman takes the paper cup of broth already at the counter's edge and drinks, exhaling hard over the rim. She wipes her mouth with her thumb, still grinning, and points at the grill for another. The camera drops to the iron as the vendor's tongs come down and fresh skewers hit the hot surface in a burst of oil and smoke, sizzling hard, the market noise rolling on all around, as time runs out. SCORE Bright playful K-indie groove from the first frame — bouncing bass, crisp funk drums, a plucky electric guitar riff. Everything cuts dead at the bite for the half-second hold: sizzle and market noise alone. Then the groove slams back with handclaps and a keyboard hook, brighter than before, riding at full energy and unresolved at the last frame. Ambience sits beneath the score throughout. AUDIO A full market underneath — overlapping voices, radios, shouted orders, sizzling from several directions, a ladle knocking a pot, the dog barking somewhere behind, rain on plastic sheeting, her laugh, the vendor's laugh — all beneath the score. No sound tied to the camera itself. STYLE LOCK Hyper-detailed photoreal. The market is alive but never crowded with distant figures — every person in frame is within a few metres of the lens, individually detailed, and doing one specific readable action. EVERY figure keeps moving — nothing stands still. Real food physics — sauce thick and irregular, clinging and breaking in uneven drips, never falling as an even string; steam and grill smoke rising in patchy uneven wisps, thicker in some places than others, never an even cloud; oil spitting only on the grill; rain beading on the puffer jacket. Her reaction is quick and involuntary rather than performed — small, fast, real. The camera orbit is smooth and continuous with no jitter or floating in close framings. The skewer, the bowl and the amount of sauce stay consistent from the moment it is served. The market stalls and their lights never leave frame. The image stays clean and fully exposed edge to edge, all four corners sharp and bright — no vignette, no dark frame edges, no goggle mask. No subtitles, no watermarks, no text. 16:9.
